one_liner: AMD's Zen-tuned forks of zlib, zstd, lz4, snappy, bzip2 and lzma behind one C API; level-9 zlib compresses about 3.7x faster.
what_it_does: A C library that vendors modified copies of seven codecs (lz4, lz4hc, zlib/deflate/gzip, zstd, bzip2, snappy, lzma) and exposes both their native APIs (zlib.h, zstd.h, LZ4_* and so on) and a unified API (aocl_llc_setup / aocl_llc_compress / aocl_llc_decompress / aocl_llc_destroy over an aocl_compression_desc handle that carries buffers, level and thread count). Output stays in each codec's standard format in single-threaded use, so existing decoders read it. An optional OpenMP build adds multi-threaded compression and decompression for all seven codecs (compression only for lzma).
how_it_is_fast: Each codec gets algorithmic and SIMD changes chosen at run time by a function-multiversioning dispatcher (SSE2, AVX, AVX2, AVX512). In zlib this means Intel's deflate_medium strategy, Konstantin Nosov's fast_zlib longest_match, x86 slide_hash, a hash table 4x larger (AOCL_ADDITIONAL_HASH_BITS 2), PCLMUL/VPCLMULQDQ CRC-32 and Chromium/zlib-ng chunk-copy inflate (chunkset_sse2/avx512). Other codecs get match-skipping heuristics (lz4, zstd, snappy), branchless snappy decompression, LZ4HC pattern analysis and fewer bzip2 Huffman refinement passes; several of these are build-time options that trade ratio for speed.
when_to_use: Server or HPC code on AMD Zen (or other x86-64) that already links zlib, bzip2 or snappy and wants faster output in the same format without changing callers: level 6-9 deflate (about 2.5-3.7x faster compress, 2x faster inflate in the vendor run) and bzip2 (about 2x compress, 1.6x decompress).
Applications that use several codecs and want one dependency with one dispatch layer and one test suite instead of seven separately tuned libraries.
Bulk compression of large buffers or files where the OpenMP build can split work across cores and the consumer either uses AOCL or skips the RAP header.
Teams that need AMD-supported builds with fuzz, ASAN and Valgrind test targets on Linux and Windows.
when_not_to_use: Non-x86 targets: the optimised paths are x86-only (SSE2 to AVX512), and lzbench's reviewer asked for the Linux/x86-64 and GNU binutils restriction to be documented.
When lz4 or zstd speed is what you need: the vendor's own run shows only +5% / +2% for lz4 and +14-21% / +8-10% for zstd, with a small ratio loss (zstd -3 31.94% versus 31.20%).
When you need the fastest deflate regardless of library: zlib-ng, ISA-L igzip or libdeflate have independent numbers and wider platform support; AOCL has no published head-to-head with them.
Many small blocks: Lzma_compressBound reserves a constant 16 KB pad per call (open issue #5), so chunked LZMA output buffers can be far larger than with peer codecs.

Projects that cannot track a vendored-codec fork: AOCL re-releases upstream security fixes on its own schedule (5.3.0 shipped zlib 1.3.1-based code; 5.3.2 moved to zlib 1.3.2 'addressing known security vulnerabilities').

integration.form: shared lib or static lib (CMake 3.13+, also GNU Make; CMake OBJECT target for embedding)
integration.dependencies: none at run time for the single-threaded build; OpenMP for AOCL_ENABLE_THREADS; GoogleTest for the test suite; Doxygen/Sphinx only for docs
integration.min_toolchain: C11; GCC 8.5+ or Clang 11.0+ on Linux; Visual Studio with ClangCl on Windows
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux and Windows (multi-threaded mode experimental on Windows); optimised paths need SSE2 at minimum and scale to AVX512
integration.thread_safety: Codec calls on separate handles/streams are independent; the dispatcher setup is global and guarded by an atomic flag or critical section, but the README warns that changing optOff/optLevel between threads calling aocl_llc_setup() is undefined behaviour, and aocl_llc_destroy resets process-wide dispatch state.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the native zlib/bzip2/snappy/lz4/zstd APIs keep upstream names and formats, so relinking works, but symbols clash with a system zlib or zstd in the same process unless built with AOCL_LLC_PREFIX, and multi-threaded output carries a non-standard RAP frame header that stock decoders must skip.

gotchas: Behaviour depends on environment variables read at first use: AOCL_DISABLE_OPT=ON forces reference paths, AOCL_ENABLE_INSTRUCTIONS caps the ISA, AOCL_ZLIB_QUICK_MODE=ON switches zlib levels 1, 2, 3 and 5 to faster settings with a worse ratio.

On Windows the CMake Release build compiles everything with /arch:AVX2, and on Linux the Snappy sources are compiled with -msse4.1 and SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32=1, so not every path honours the 'portable down to SSE2' dispatch claim.

GCC 15 needs per-file workaround flags (-fno-schedule-insns2 and others) on zlib chunkset_avx512.c and zstd_decompress_block.c; 5.3.2 notes fix 'GCC 15 decompression regressions in ZLIB and ZSTD' and 'LZ4 multi-threaded decompression data corruption', so pin 5.3.2 or later.

aocl_llc_setup() only reports excluded or unsupported codecs, not allocation failures (lzbench review concern 4), and aocl_lzma_compress() does not check the output size up front and can underflow when outsize < LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (issue #5).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over zlib-ng or the Cloudflare zlib fork when you also want bzip2 and snappy speedups and AMD support from one library; pick zlib-ng, libdeflate or ISA-L igzip when you only need deflate, need ARM, or want independently measured numbers. For bzip2-compatible output it is faster per thread in the vendor run (about 2.1x) than lbzip2's catalogued 1.6x, though the two were measured on different machines.
verified_claims_summary: In an AMD developer's lzbench pull request (#321, unmerged, changes requested), single-threaded on an AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370 with boost off, GCC 15.2.0, silesia.tar, aocl-zlib 5.3.0 -9 compressed at 27.47 MB/s and decompressed at 439.38 MB/s versus zlib 1.3.2 at 7.37 and 212.55 MB/s (ratio 32.21% versus 31.91%); aocl-bzip2 -9 ran 20.58 / 37.65 versus 8.92 / 23.16 MB/s and aocl-snappy 413 / 1434 versus 343 / 719 MB/s. The run used AOCL 5.3.0, which the 5.3.2 release notes say had GCC 15 decompression regressions in zlib and zstd, so the numbers may not match the fixed release.
status_note: Actively maintained by AMD (v5.3.2 released 2026-08-20, regular releases since 4.1) under file-by-file BSD-3-Clause, MIT and NCSA plus upstream codec licences; usable as a library, but it is a vendor fork that lags upstream codec releases and has little outside adoption (44 stars).
